term: actual-node source-path or injective anchored regress and world labels
definition: SourcePath G x is existence of s with the existing FiniteCausalPath G.edge x s and Graph.Source s. This finite path walks upstream, opposite the causal arrows; its zero-length same case at a source is not a self-cause. AnchoredRegress G x is a function f:Nat→Node with f0=x, injective, and edge f(n+1) (fn) for all n. On an actualGraph every node of both paths/chains exists in the same fixed world. Nat indices count positions, not temporal instants. StarterWorlds m consists of worlds with some actual Graph.Source, not a source for every node or a temporal first event. RegressWorlds m consists of worlds with some actual anchored injective regress. WorldClassification conjoins the pointwise source-path-or-regress coverage, equality of the populated-world set {w | ∃x,ExistsAt w x} with StarterWorlds∪RegressWorlds, and a source in every world with finite actual carrier and explicit population. Empty worlds have neither label; finite candidate domains are not silently assumed. The horns and world sets may overlap. SourcePath is not Acc; accessibility excludes all infinite predecessor chains, while one source path can coexist with another infinite branch.
note: Classical Mathlib source/chain selection is used under the approved three-axiom policy. Acyclicity makes a descending chain injective. No finite branching, bounded past length, temporal beginning, modal accessibility, union-WF, necessary being or divine uniqueness is inferred. FinitelyGroundedPower is used internally only for its parameterized induction/path extraction.
